title: Human Expert Evaluation of Agentic AI for EO, form F21
description:
Thank you for helping us evaluate the performance of different LLMs in Agentic AI frameworks for EO!

WHAT THIS IS
We built a benchmark to test the performance of different LLMs in agentic settings. This evaluation form is to compare the answers given by these LLMs when answering a question using different tools related to the agentic framework that we built - including different EO endpoints (Copernicus/Sentinel, Landsat), ERA5 climate data, EO Dashboard narratives, ESA science strategy documents, GIS analysis and scientific literature search.

You will be given 8 questions, and for each question you see every anonymous answer that assistant actually produced for it -- usually several, occasionally just one if only one assistant answered that particular question.

WHAT YOU DO
(About 42 minutes for this form -- your progress is saved in this browser, so it's fine to do this over more than one sitting.) The form will guide you through it, but for every question you will
1. Rate how relevant and realistic the question is for EO users.
2. Score the accuracy of each answer shown.
3. If there's more than one answer, rank them all from best to worst (skip this step when only one answer is shown -- there's nothing to compare it to).

HOW TO JUDGE ACCURACY
Judge scientific and domain correctness, and whether the answer addresses every part of the question. A minority of answers (marked "▣ image" next to the answer letter) include the actual image the assistant looked at -- check the description against it directly. For every other answer you cannot open the files or images it says it produced: treat claims that you find implausible or unsupported as errors. Do not reward length or formatting. If you cannot judge a question, say so in the comment field and give your best estimate.

Answers were produced automatically and may contain errors. Local file paths were removed from the answers. Long answers are collapsed by default — click an answer to expand it.

PRIVACY
Your name is recorded so we can follow up if needed, and is not shown to other experts. Responses are used only for the research evaluation of this benchmark and are reported in aggregate. Participation is voluntary; you can stop at any time by closing the page.

profile_fields.title: Name
profile_fields.help: So we know who a response came from. Not shown to other experts.

profile_fields.title: How would you rate your Earth Observation expertise?
Which areas are you experienced in?
choices: Climate and atmospheric data (ERA5, trace gases)

profile_fields.title: Consent
choices: I agree that my responses are used for the research evaluation of this benchmark.

relevance.title: How relevant and realistic is this question for EO users (researchers, analysts, practitioners)?
relevance.help: 1 = not relevant or unrealistic; 3 = plausible but marginal or somewhat artificial; 5 = highly relevant and realistic.

accuracy.title: Accuracy: how correct and complete is each answer?
accuracy.help: 1 = incorrect or unusable; 2 = mostly incorrect or major omissions; 3 = partially correct or incomplete; 4 = mostly correct, minor issues; 5 = correct and complete. Equal scores are allowed.

ranking.title: Ranking: order all answers from best to worst.
ranking.help: Drag, or use the arrows, to put the best answer at the top and the worst at the bottom. Ties are not allowed.

familiarity.title: How familiar are you with the topic of this question?

comment.title: Comment (optional)
comment.help: For example: an error you spotted, why a question is not relevant, or that you could not judge it.

answers.text:
Here are the relevant CDS (Copernicus Data Space) datasets and methods for downloading Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI atmospheric composition data:

1. Sentinel-5P L2 Products via CDSE (Sentinel Hub)
• Collection: Sentinel-5P L2 (Level 2) products
• Data Types: Trace gases, aerosols, and cloud data (e.g., NO₂, CO, O₃, SO₂, CH₄, HCHO, aerosol index, cloud fraction).
• Access Methods:
  • Sentinel Hub API (via CDSE):
    Use the fetch_sentinel5p_l2 tool with parameters like:

    fetch_sentinel5p_l2(
        bbox=[west, south, east, north],  # Bounding box (e.g., [10, 40, 15, 45])

items.question: What CDS datasets are available for accessing ERA5 reanalysis data?

answers.text:
The Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) provides the following ERA5 reanalysis datasets for access:

1. ERA5-Land: High-resolution reanalysis dataset for land surface variables.
2. ERA5: The fifth generation of ECMWF atmospheric reanalysis of the global climate, providing hourly estimates of various atmospheric variables.
3. ERA5 monthly averaged data: Monthly mean values of ERA5 reanalysis parameters.
4. ERA5.1: An updated version of ERA5, addressing identified issues.
5. ERA5 back extension: Extends ERA5 data back to 1950 for select variables.
6. ERA5 ocean: Ocean-related variables from ERA5.

These datasets can be accessed via the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) (https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/).

The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE) provides access to ERA5 reanalysis data through several datasets. Here are the key datasets available for accessing ERA5 data on the CDSE:

1. ERA5 Monthly Averaged Data on Single Levels
   • This dataset provides monthly averages of atmospheric, land, and oceanic climate variables. It is useful for long-term climate analysis and trend studies.

2. ERA5 Monthly Averaged Data on Pressure Levels
   • This dataset contains monthly averages of atmospheric variables at various pressure levels. It is ideal for studying atmospheric dynamics, vertical profiles, and weather patterns.

3. ERA5 Hourly Data on Single Levels
   • This dataset offers hourly estimates of atmospheric, land, and oceanic climate variables. It is suitable for detailed weather analysis, short-term forecasting, and high-resolution climate studies.

4. ERA5 Hourly Data on Pressure Levels
   • This dataset provides hourly estimates of atmospheric variables at various pressure levels. It is useful for analyzing atmospheric conditions, weather systems, and vertical structures.

5. ERA5 Land Monthly Averaged Data
   • This dataset includes monthly averages of land variables such as temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture. It is valuable for land surface and hydrological studies.

6. ERA5 Land Hourly Data
   • This dataset offers hourly estimates of land variables. It is ideal for detailed land surface analysis, including soil moisture, evaporation, and runoff.

7. ERA5 Climate Data Store (CDS) Tools
   • The CDSE also provides tools and APIs for accessing and processing ERA5 data, allowing users to extract, analyze, and visualize the data according to their needs.

These datasets are available for download and analysis through the CDSE platform, providing researchers, scientists, and policymakers with comprehensive access to high-quality reanalysis data for climate and weather studies.

The Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) provides the following ERA5 reanalysis datasets for access:

1. ERA5-Land: High-resolution reanalysis dataset for land surface variables.
2. ERA5: The fifth generation of ECMWF atmospheric reanalysis of the global climate, providing hourly estimates of various atmospheric variables.
3. ERA5 monthly averaged data: Monthly mean values of ERA5 reanalysis parameters.
4. ERA5.1: An updated version of ERA5, addressing identified issues.
5. ERA5 back extension: Extends ERA5 data back to 1950 for select variables.
6. ERA5 ocean: Ocean-related variables from ERA5.

These datasets can be accessed via the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) (https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/).

• Single Levels (Surface/Screen-level):
    • reanalysis-era5-single-levels: Hourly data (1940–present).
    • reanalysis-era5-single-levels-monthly-means: Monthly mean data (1940–present).
• Pressure Levels (Atmospheric Profiles):
    • reanalysis-era5-pressure-levels: Hourly data on 37 pressure levels (1940–present).
    • reanalysis-era5-pressure-levels-monthly-means: Monthly mean data on pressure levels (1940–present).

• derived-era5-single-levels-daily-statistics: Daily mean, max, min, and sum for surface variables.
• derived-era5-pressure-levels-daily-statistics: Daily statistics for pressure-level variables.

4. Specialized ERA5-Derived Data
• sis-agrometeorological-indicators: Daily indicators derived from ERA5 specifically for agricultural applications (1979–present).
